claim: Ferry B1 runs year-round to Hovedøya, Bleikøya, Gressholmen, Lindøya, Nakholmen; B2 is summer-only; one-day Ruter pass ~132 NOK covers ferries plus city transit; Oslo Pass holders ride free.
quote: A one-day pass costs around 132 NOK ... This standard transit ticket covers unlimited ferry access plus city bus travel. Oslo Pass holders receive ferry rides at no additional cost.

claim: Ruter's regular zone tickets are valid on all island ferry routes (B1 to Bleikøya/Gressholmen/Lindøya/Nakholmen, B1X summer extra to Hovedøya, B2 to Langøyene).
quote: Ruter's regular tickets are valid on all boat routes.

claim: Hovedøya pairs 12th-century Cistercian monastery ruins with swimmable western rocks; Lindøya is the postcard island with ~300 colourful early-1900s cabins and two designated swim spots; Gressholmen is a nature reserve with sheltered bays and Gressholmen Kro tavern; Langøyene has the inner fjord's only sandy beach with water hitting 23–24 °C in July.
quote: Langøyene ... the only sandy beach with free camping in the inner fjord ... sandy bottom that retains heat reaching 23–24°C in July.

claim: The Hovedøya ferry crossing from Aker Brygge takes only 5–10 minutes, and a loop walk around the island takes about 45 minutes; the Cistercian monastery was founded in 1147 by English monks.
quote: A walking trail circles the island in about 45 minutes ... Hovedøya Abbey, a Cistercian monastery founded in 1147 by monks from England.

claim: Take T-bane Line 1 toward Frognerseteren, exit at Holmenkollen station, then a ~10-minute uphill walk to the jump and museum; combined museum + tower entry runs 140 NOK adult / 70 NOK child and is included with Oslo Pass; summer hours 9 am–8 pm.
quote: Museum and tower entry costs 140NOK (approximately £12) for adults and 70NOK (roughly £6) for children under 18. The Oslo Pass includes free admission ... summer hours (June-August) from 9am-8pm.

claim: From Holmenkollen station the well-marked uphill walk to the jump is about 10–15 minutes; the redesigned 2010 jump rises 64 m and an elevator runs to the tower's panoramic deck.
quote: From central Oslo, take Metro Line 1 (Frognerseteren line) to Holmenkollen station, from where it's an uphill walk of about 10–15 minutes along well-marked paths.

claim: The Frognerseteren–Øvresetertjern–Holmenkollen trail is a roughly 3-mile easy forest hike taking 1.5–2 hours, typically walked downhill from Frognerseteren (the line-1 terminus) back to Holmenkollen station.
quote: easy hike that covers 3 miles with an elevation gain of 180 feet, taking about 1.5–2 hours to complete.

claim: The optional Kollensvevet zipline is a 361 m line with a 107 m drop from the jump's top, costs 829 NOK including museum entry, with a 40 kg minimum (tandem under that).
quote: The zipline costs 829 NOK per person and includes entrance to the ski museum ... children under 40 kilos must jump in tandem with an adult.

claim: Ekebergparken is reached by tram 13 or 19 toward Ljabru, stopping at Ekebergparken or Sportsplassen; the main viewpoint, Utsikten, is the spot that inspired Munch's Scream; the basic loop takes 60–90 minutes, longer if lingering.
quote: Take tram 13 or 19 toward Ljabru and get off at Ekebergparken or Sportsplassen ... Ekeberg is where Munch found the mood and skyline that fed his most famous painting ... You can see a lot in 60 to 90 minutes.

claim: Ekebergparken opened in September 2013 on a 25.5-acre (~10 ha) forested ridge in southeast Oslo with 31 inaugural sculptures (financier Christian Ringnes set aside NOK 350 million for an eventual 80), free public access.
quote: inaugurated 26 September 2013 ... 31 sculptures ... wooded area spans 25.5 acres (about 10 hectares) ... panoramic view of the city at Ekeberg.

claim: Marina Abramović's 2013 work The Scream at Ekebergparken posed 270 Oslo residents in front of the exact landscape that inspired Munch's Skrik; a film of the performance plays permanently at the Ekeberg Museum.
quote: posed in front of the very same landscape that inspired Munch's famous motif.
